Sorry, it's been a long week.  And yes HK, IREP's effectiveness is diminished somewhat by the draw-two rule, but then it's also increased since it causes you to draw yourself.  I may consider having Visionary's cards include a "that deck does not apply the draw-two rule on its next card play" rider, but IREP definitely does not.  Improved chances of getting Impromptu Invention are more than enough help to give the Wraith.

EXT. NIGHT - ROOK CITY SLUMS

As the shambling figures are engulfed in flame, they do not scream, but simply collapse into blackened heaps.  Abruptly, the heroes see a slim FIGURE leaning nonchalantly against the far wall of the still-steaming alley, its voluminous blue robe concealing all but a pallidly attractive female face. 

PALE CULTIST:  "Congratulations, oh Knight in Shining Machinery; you're a mass murderer!  True, these unfortunate victims were the Worthiest of our Lord, those who have fully given in to despair and accepted the inevitability of their impending demise.  But that fact will mean nothing in court; they still had names and homes and social security cards, and once their dental records are identified by the dedicated crusaders-for-justice of the Rook City Police Department, you'll all be lucky to escape criminal charges, and at the very least can look forward to a Wrongful Death lawsuit.  It may not be Our Way, but these are trying times, and we must adapt to whatever tools our adversaries give us.  Good luck trying to convince a judge that the people you just incinerated were 'the walking dead'.  We live in faithless times; no one will believe you, and I of course will deny everything.  Tell me, how does it feel to know that you cannot escape the trap of your own hypocritical laws?"

Rook City

The rustic-looking drum the deceased were carrying is oddly almost untouched by the fire (and by ABSOLUTE ZERO's little zap); as it falls from between the nerveless fingers of the last two "zombies", it hits the pavement and issues an eerie, resonating "BOOOOOOOM…".  The sound seems to echo inside each of the listeners' skulls, and few of them can avoid displaying a grimace or uttering a grunt of pain; the CULTIST however is clearly unaffected.  As the sound dies away, the heroes suddenly see why the drum fell several seconds after its bearers were barbecued in place…one of the charred hulks that was supporting it just made a fist.

CULTIST:  "Well okay, almost no proof.  I will have to figure out how my testimony will account for your wounds sustained after you slew your innocent victims.  Perhaps I'll tell them you fell to quarreling among yourselves and came to blows; that always seems to happen with you 'super' types."

As the woman continues describing how she and her friends will make you look insane in a court of law, you unquestionably see the thick layer of soot fossilizing one of the blackened bodies break in several places, then the "corpse" begins taking several halting, jerky, marionette-like steps toward Legacy.  Though steeled against the mind-splitting sound of the drum, he was distracted enough by it that he doesn't think to react, and before he even notices the skeletonized figure is still moving, it is upon him, pummeling at his flesh with its carbonized hands.  The champion is too preoccupied with the zombie's more obvious attacks to notice as a tiny bone pin, tipped with a dark-red garnet, squirms of its own accord out of a pocket in the roasted cultist's former clothes, hooks itself into the fibers of his costume, and begins to "walk" like an inchworm by flexing itself until it wriggles through one hole in the fabric so that it can make another one.  In this mode, it travels rapidly around to the rear of his leg and then up the back side of his body, unerringly proceeding toward the nape of his neck.
